instructions: Drain the chickpeas in a colander and rinse them under cold water. Shake them dry and transfer them into a large serving bowl.
Peel the onion and chop it as finely as you can. Chop both peppers finely too.
In a medium bowl, whisk the 1/3 cup oil, the 3 tbsp sherry vinegar and the salt together.
Add the onion and peppers to the dressing and stir.
Pour it over the chickpeas and toss well. Let it sit for 15 minutes, or longer in the fridge.
Serve it cold or at room temperature. To pack it, keep it in a jar in the fridge for up to 3 days.
method_notes: Invitado de Invierno (Miriam Garcia) dresses cooked chickpeas with finely chopped red and green pepper, red onion, olive oil and a little sherry vinegar, and lets the salad sit so the chickpeas take on the dressing. Her recipe cooks dried chickpeas and serves four as a starter, so this version uses canned chickpeas and triples the amounts for a lunch. Only the lead was readable (5.0 from 2 ratings, so it is a fallback). The 3 day fridge time is a cautious figure for a dressed bean salad.
